subject: Aurion RFP — commit hedging, burst bucket, and convertibility
messages:
From: Marco Deluca <marco@aurion.ai>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFP: capacity smoothing & burst pricing (Aurion)

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for taking a look at our RFP. Attached is the procurement packet and our commercial appendix. A few commercial questions for Redwood that are critical to our vendor scoring:

1) Commit hedging: Aurion expects month-to-month usage variance up to +150% on traffic spikes. Do you offer a hedging or reserve-credit mechanism that lets us cover peaks without paying the sustained overage rate? If so, how is it priced and reconciled?

2) Burst bucket convertibility: Can short-term "burst" credits be converted to reserved capacity (or applied toward committed baseline) mid-term if usage proves sustained? Is there an API/contract path for conversion?

3) Per-model token tiers: We use a mix of smaller encoder models for embeddings, mid-size for classification, and large decoder models for generative features. Please outline per-1k token pricing for each model tier and the overage price for unexpected spikes.

4) KV-cache and session slot pricing: Several of our LLM features rely on long-lived sessions with large KV caches. Do you charge extra for persistent KV cache usage or is it included in token accounting?

5) Escrow/prepaid credits: Aurion prefers prefunding for budget control. Do you support an escrow/prepaid bucket with a discount schedule and contractually guaranteed convertibility? What are the options for term discounts?

I'm copying procurement in case they want to follow with the questionnaire. Goal: vendor selection by the week of Apr 8.

Attachments: aurion_rfp.pdf, aurion_procurement_questionnaire.docx

Regards,
Marco
Head of Platform, Aurion AI

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Marco Deluca <marco@aurion.ai>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-31T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: capacity smoothing & burst pricing (Aurion)

Marco — thanks for the clear questions and the packet. Below is a concise commercial proposal that addresses each ask; I've attached a one-page pricing summary and a starter SOW for procurement.

High-level approach (summary):
- Baseline monthly committed tokens: start-of-term committed baseline (e.g., 150M tokens/month). Committed rate applies to sustained usage inside the baseline.
- Smoothing window & true-up: a rolling 90-day smoothing window with quarterly true-ups. Credits consumed within the smoothing window are priced at the committed rate; sustained overages after the window trigger true-up reconciliation.
- Burst bucket (short-term credits): an optional preapproved burst bucket that covers short spikes at a premium discount relative to standard overage. Example: burst credits priced at 0.75x the public overage rate for the first X tokens within a 24–72 hour window.
- Hedge/Reserve credits: a prepaid reserve (hedge) bucket you can purchase at a discounted rate (e.g., 0.65x committed price) that can be drawn against for spikes. Hedge bucket can be partially converted into committed baseline at quarterly checkpoints (conversion requires 30 days notice and prorated accounting).
- Overage mechanics: after smoothing window and any applicable burst/hedge draws, overages bill at the overage rate by model tier. Overage rate tiers are shown in the attached spreadsheet.
- Model-tier pricing (examples from sheet):
  * Embedding-tier (family E-small/E-medium): $0.40 / 1k tokens committed; $0.60 / 1k overage
  * Mid-tier (classification/semantic): $0.80 / 1k tokens committed; $1.20 / 1k overage
  * Large generative (decoder long-context): $3.25 / 1k tokens committed; $4.50 / 1k overage
- KV cache & session slots: persistent KV cache usage is accounted for via session slot licensing on Dedicated and via a KV-credit multiplier on Hosted. For Hosted (our standard offering), large persistent KV increases count toward an effective "session token" meter (details in sheet). For Dedicated we can offer fixed session-slot bundles (no per-token surcharge).
- Escrow / prepaid credits: supported. We offer prepaid buckets with tiered discounts tied to term and commit level (1–12 months). Prepaid credits live in escrow and can be applied to either overages or converted to baseline at quarterly checkpoints subject to conversion fees (~2–5% to prevent churn abuse).
- SLA & credits: standard SLAs apply; for commercial deals we can negotiate enhanced SLA credits tied to monthly uptime and per-request latency buckets.

Operational notes:
- Conversion process: API + contract amendment; conversion is subject to accounting reconciliation and a single-sided notice period.
- Line-item transparency: per-route cost breakdown available in Redwood Console for chargebacks and internal chargebacks.
- Procurement docs included: starter SOW, pricing XLSX, example order form.

Next steps / asks:
1) Confirm preferred term (12 vs 24 months) and target baseline tokens so we can produce a numeric proposal + DocuSign.
2) Do you want the prepaid (hedge) bucket enabled at kickoff or staged after Q1 true-up?
3) Can procurement provide the contract/PO template or should Redwood propose the first draft?

Attachments: redwood_pricing_spreadsheet_v1.xlsx, redwood_sow_draft_v0.3.pdf

Happy to hop on a 30-min call this week. Proposed times: Thu Mar 31 10:00–11:30 PT or Fri Apr 1 14:00–16:00 PT.

—Aisha
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marco Deluca <marco@aurion.ai>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@aurion.ai>
Date: 2028-04-02T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: capacity smoothing & burst pricing (Aurion)

Aisha — this is helpful. A few clarifying items from procurement and engineering:

- Convertibility timing: procurement needs an explicit SLA that allows conversion of prepaid hedge credits to baseline within a maximum 45-day window and a defined accounting method (how unused hedge credits are pro-rated). Can Redwood accept a conversion SLA?

- Dedicated vs Hosted KV cost: engineering asks whether the Dedicated session-slot bundles can be priced as an add-on to Hosted during the pilot. Essentially: can we trial dedicated-style session slots on Hosted without moving to a Dedicated cluster?

- Example numbers: for scoring we need a worked example: 150M committed tokens, 300M peak month (one month only), 24-month term, with a $500k prepaid hedge at kickoff. Could you return a worked pricing scenario showing the net cost in month of peak and across quarter reconciliation?

Procurement has attached a short questionnaire (see aurion_procurement_questionnaire.docx). Procurement is leaning toward 24 months if the hedge convertibility SLA is acceptable.

Thanks — can you loop in anyone on your side for legal/procurement?

Best,
Marco

Marco / procurement — looping in Vivek (VP Sales) and Priyom (Solutions) to confirm the commitments and to fast-track a worked example. Short answers first, followed by immediate next steps:

Short answers:
- Conversion SLA: Redwood can commit to a conversion window of 30–45 days (contract-configurable). We'll include a pro-rata accounting example in the worked scenario.
- Trialing session-slot behavior on Hosted: we can provide a Hosted "session-slot" emulation during pilot (limited to X concurrent slots and a temporary billing flag) for 90 days. If you need dedicated hardware semantics, we'll map that to Dedicated pricing after pilot.
- Worked example: we'll produce a spreadsheet showing 150M committed, 300M one-month spike, 24-month term, and a $500k hedge draw. Deliverable by EOD Apr 6.

Mutual action plan (MAP):
